passage:
A town created an app for a walking tour of historic streets. Visitors could hear stories when they reached certain places.
The app was popular, but one guide worried people would stop joining human tours.
Instead, something different happened. Many visitors used the app first, then joined a guide to ask deeper questions.
The guide realized the app gave basic information, while human guides gave conversation, humor, and local memory.
The town kept both.
Technology did not end the human tour. It changed what visitors expected from it. When basic facts are easy to get, human guides become valuable for what machines cannot provide: connection and judgment.
